text:
Bitcoin remains pressured in the $62,200–$63,000 corridor the morning of June 24, weighed down by an exhausting six-week streak of net spot ETF redemptions that has drained up to $8 billion from the ecosystem. This sustained institutional caution is heavily influenced by a broader macroeconomic "risk-off" posture, triggered by Tuesday's violent 2.2% Nasdaq contraction as investors rapidly derisked from extended AI and semiconductor valuations.

Despite the cyclical price weakness, structural regulatory milestones continue apace in Europe. NAGA Group and Ripple successfully advanced their MiCA-compliant Crypto Asset Service Provider (CASP) authorizations, cementing their footholds ahead of the critical July 1 EU compliance deadline.

The broader market narrative is currently dictated by a flight to safety. With the U.S. Manufacturing PMI unexpectedly accelerating to 55.7 and front-end Treasury yields like the 6-month bill stabilizing near 3.96%, risk-free rates remain attractive enough to suppress speculative digital asset bids.
